# Executive Workshop Proposal for Tamarack Instruments

Prepared for Dana Whitfield, General Counsel and budget holder

## Situation Summary

Tamarack Instruments designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments. It is headquartered in the Netherlands and operates in the Netherlands, Germany and the United States. The Client currently runs a customer service chatbot on its support portal, is piloting AI visual inspection on the German production line and plans to introduce AI sales forecasting next year. An internal audit finding in June 2026 recorded that the Client holds no inventory of AI systems.

You have stated the objective plainly: "I want governance in place before visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027." The regulatory drivers you named are the EU AI Act and GDPR. Work toward ISO/IEC 42001 is expected to begin next year, although the start date is not yet fixed.

The Client already operates an ISO/IEC 27001 information security management system and an ISO 9001 quality management system. Three constraints shape the work. Customer data must stay in the EU. The German works council must be consulted before anything touches production staff. Budget is approved up to US$80,000 this fiscal year.

## Why a One-Day Executive Session Fits Now

Tamarack Instruments is at the piloting stage. At this stage the most consequential governance choices are still open and still inexpensive to make. Those choices include who owns AI governance, how much AI risk the Client will accept and how oversight will run. Once visual inspection moves into production, the same choices become harder to change.

A single day lets the leadership group make those choices together. It does not commit the Client to a longer engagement before the direction is agreed. Your timeline records a decision expected by 15 December 2026. The workshop date is `Unknown` until agreed. If the session is held before that date, its decision log and draft roadmap are available to inform that decision.

The workshop also gives the June 2026 audit finding a clear executive response. It places that response within the frameworks the Client already runs, so it does not create a parallel structure.

## Workshop Structure and Emphasis for Tamarack Instruments

The day runs as four 90-minute blocks. It draws on the GRC Workbook (https://github.com/rolldabones/grc-workbook) and Slow AI Kitchen (https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen).

**Block 1, Alignment.** The group reviews the Client's current AI posture through the three use cases and the audit finding on the missing AI inventory. The aim is a shared view of what is deployed, what is in pilot and what is planned. The block produces a shared statement of governance intent anchored to the Q2 2027 production milestone for visual inspection.

**Block 2, Principles.** The group sets governance operating principles. These include the three Academy principles: Slow AI, Informed Intent, Final Liability rests with the Human. Each is applied to the Client's context:

- Slow AI is tested against the gate between the visual inspection pilot and production.
- Informed Intent is tested against the chatbot already in service and the planned forecasting system.
- Final Liability rests with the Human is tested against the question of who accepts AI outputs and on what criteria. The Definition of Done (https://github.com/rolldabones/definition-of-done) serves as the acceptance-layer reference.

The room ranks the agreed principles.

**Block 3, Roadmap.** The group sequences governance work against the EU AI Act, GDPR and the ISO/IEC 42001 target, positioning AI governance as an extension of the ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS and the ISO 9001 quality management system. The Profile names these frameworks but does not state which registers, procedures or records exist within them. The specific attachment points are therefore `Unknown` and will be confirmed in session rather than assumed.

Two dependencies are also placed on the roadmap:

- **Works council consultation.** Whether visual inspection touches production staff is `Unknown`, so the roadmap places the consultation as a dependency to be confirmed.
- **EU data residency.** Where the chatbot processes and stores data is `Unknown`, so the roadmap includes confirming how the EU data residency constraint applies to the chatbot and to future systems.

Regulatory classification of each use case is orientation only, and each item is flagged for confirmation with external counsel. The block produces a draft 12-month roadmap with owners drawn from the roles in the room.

**Block 4, Decisions.** The group records executive decisions on governance ownership, risk appetite for AI, oversight cadence and budget mandate within the approved US$80,000. AI Governance for Boards (https://github.com/rolldabones/ai-governance-for-boards) serves as the reference for structuring oversight above the executive layer. Whether the Client reports AI matters to a board is `Unknown`.

The block closes with *The Turtle and the Phoenix* and the twenty-minute closing exercise from its facilitation kit (https://github.com/rolldabones/AI-Governance-Academy/blob/main/the-turtle-and-the-phoenix.md). This closing exercise is the retention device for the three principles.

## Deliverables

After the workshop the Client receives three documents:

- **Decision log.** Records each decision with its owner, rationale and review date.
- **Prioritized roadmap.** The 12-month roadmap as agreed in the room, with owners and dependencies, including the works council and data residency items.
- **Readiness observations.** Observations drawn from the GRC Workbook domains of governance structures, inventories, risk management, policies and evidence. They describe what the session surfaced. They are not an audit opinion, and they make no prediction about ISO/IEC 42001 certification or any audit outcome. Regulatory items in all three documents carry a note to confirm with external counsel.

## Logistics and Price

The Executive Workshop is one day, delivered live and virtually as four 90-minute blocks with breaks. It is designed for executive leadership and the roles named in discovery: General Counsel, CISO, Head of Quality, Head of Data, German plant manager and two internal auditors.

Confirmed attendance is `Unknown`. Participant locations are also `Unknown`, so the session's time zone will be set once attendees are confirmed.

The fee is US$7,500, which sits within the US$80,000 approved for this fiscal year.

## Next Step

We propose a short call to agree the workshop date relative to your 15 December 2026 decision and to confirm attendees. We would also like to confirm which existing ISMS and quality management system artifacts you can share as pre-reads. Once these are agreed, participants receive a pre-work packet ahead of the session so the day can be spent on decisions rather than discovery.

Human-made, for Easy Work, Simply Done.
